messages.author: c8fe4075ec631c03
messages.subject: Suggest: Reactive IO
parts:
Hi,

  I have already started discussing this, but I would like to be able to place 'reactive IO' in UI.R.

  For example: inputOutputTextField("myname") 

  They would not typically have a default value specified in UI.R

  In server.R there would be:

  input
  output
  variable

  Where variables behave like reactiveValues - they can be written from and read to.

  Writing to a variable$myname would update the text in the UI.  

  It would also make the updated value available to all consumers of variable$myname, which would be automatically invoked as per the reactive mechanism.

  There might be a concept of an initial value function

  variableInit$myname = variableText({  
    system.today()
  })

Use case 1:

  UI.R wants to contain a date field, which should have the value 'today', or the most recent ticket number.

  Since UI.R is fixed it may be hard to do this, or the data for the current user might not be available.

  server.R variable functions could do this easily.

Use Case 2:

  An input variable may have a number of valid values which is smaller than the set of values the user could input.  If the user inputs an invalid value, the value in the client should change to the nearest value value.

  server.R would take the value and (e.g.) round it, which would update the UI.  Note that race conditions between the user typing and the server updating may need to be dealt with.

Use Case 3:

  A change to a different input may be able to supply a new default value to the first input.

Alternative 1:

  reactiveUI or renderUI can be used to do this, but they are heavyweight and it slows down application start up.

  also the input values generated by inputs embedded in renderUI must pass from the server to the client and back before the server can take any action based upon them.  This has the effect of the application waking up panel by panel, which isn't as smart looking as I'd like.

  reactiveUI created inputs are created afresh each time the reactiveUI updates, which may create problems for e.g. javascript capturing events from those inputs.

Alternative 2:
  
  Javascript magic with hidden output fields being able to update input fields..  

  This is how I currently handle it, but it hardly fits with the ease of use of the rest of shiny.  It also has some unpleasant possibilities for race conditions.

-Alex

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Suggest: Reactive IO
parts:
These are excellent ideas which Winston and I have begun discussing as well. We want to make sure we design it carefully because as you point out there is the potential for race conditions and other edge cases that we want to make sure we at least know about.

If we get it "right" though, there's a chance the current notions of "input" and "output" won't be necessary anymore (though we would obviously want to provide backwards compatibility for today's Shiny apps). An input could just be a variable that happens never to be set from the server (other than the initial value), and an output could be a variable that the client never changes.

I am very excited by this line of thinking but we'll definitely be proceeding at a deliberate pace. In the meantime if you continue experimenting with Shiny we're happy to keep learning from your experiences!
